## Teaching Philosophy

I view mathematics and statistics as disciplines that are best learned through a combination of conceptual understanding, structured problem solving, and practical application.

In teaching, I aim to help students move beyond memorizing formulas or procedures and instead understand:

- Why a method works
- When it should be used
- What assumptions it relies on
- How to interpret results
- How to communicate reasoning clearly

I also believe students learn quantitative material best when they are encouraged to ask questions, work through examples, and connect abstract ideas to concrete problems.
